authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10158 mukha explicitly gives mouth/face mu/muh and retained-kh mukha forms. The simple survey moho/māī and mukh responses preserve these attested contractions or learned/regional forms. Reviewed comparison: H muh “mouth” (f_mkp6eo4tqrngu). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

Survey ordinary vowel/gender variants retain this black adjective; karḍo/kaḍo needs separate extension analysis. Reviewed comparison: H karo “black” (f_shjrvnp3ustfw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: H mara “he killed” (f_kdehpp7h6ebyo). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6507.2 *dekṣati gives the dekh- see verb and regional v-/d- variation through transmission. Dekh-ta, dekh-u and ordinary -y past forms retain that stem; dekh-liyo requires the take light verb to be analyzed. Reviewed comparison: Dang dekʰnu “he sees; he saw” (f_cxv7xeg25h72u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
